title: M60 lua LUA-01 — every lua relationship carries the line of its name-bearing node
rationale: LUA-01: 0 of 15 lua relationships carried any line field while java emitted line_number:2 through the identical pipeline, so the M60 matrix reads lua `lines: n/a`. The rule is M59 (#825)'s, not invented here: the line is where the NAME is written, not where the enclosing node starts. The multi-line call in the fixture is the falsifier — a whole-line implementation passes every other row and fails it.

fixture.lines.lua:
-- fixture: every relationship kind, and the multi-line call that breaks
-- a whole-line implementation of the rule
local helper = function() return 1 end
function caller()
  helper()
  local obj = {}
  obj
    .method()
end
local Account = {}
setmetatable(Account, AccountMeta)
AccountMeta = {}
function Account:new() end
function Account:make()
  local inst = Account:new()
  return inst
end
local mod = require("some.module")
return mod

checks.name: the multi-line call is a real trap in this fixture (callee line != receiver line)
every emitted relationship carries a line
every predicted edge carries the line of its name-bearing node
the multi-line call is NOT reported at the receiver's line
each contains edge agrees with its symbol's declaration line
the unmutated analyzer passes every expectation

detail.name: the line is not emitted at all (the pre-fix state)
failures: edge with no line: calls caller->helper
edge with no line: calls caller->method

detail.name: whole-line: the receiver's line instead of the callee's
failures: calls caller->method expected L8 got L7

detail.name: off-by-one: a 0-based line
failures: calls caller->helper expected L5 got L4
calls caller->method expected L8 got L7

detail.name: LUA-13 again: a multi-line snippet as the target (filtered away downstream)
failures: calls caller->method expected L8 got NO EDGE/LINE

detail.name: a contains edge disagrees with its symbol's line
failures: contains caller->obj expected L6 got L99
contains caller->obj edge L99 vs symbol L6

mutants.method: OUTPUT mutation, not source mutation. The engine caches analyzer modules, so editing the source after first import has no effect: the first draft of this suite planted 4/4 regressions and caught 0/4 because every mutant re-measured the unmutated analyzer. Output mutation also tests the right thing — the legs are about what the pipeline emits, not how the source is spelled — and matches how script/m60/verify-910-c-includes.ts mutates index rows.

limitations: Expected lines are hand-authored, then re-derived at run time by locating the callee's line in the fixture text so a fixture edit cannot silently invalidate an expectation. A systematic misreading of the M59 contract would still pass.
The gate covers five relationship kinds. A NEW kind the analyzer starts emitting is caught by the 'every emitted relationship carries a line' leg, but has no expected line until one is added here.

Output mutation proves the verification logic can fail. It does NOT prove the analyzer source produces the right output for any mutant, because the engine caches the module — a source-level mutation test would need one fresh process per mutant, and is owed.
